reason: Schedule and feasibility lens. The CPU part fits the calendar: Ultrack on all 199 clips can finish on free Kaggle CPU kernels by 26 Sep morning. The idea still fails on two counts. First, it only feeds ideas 1/2, which were both refuted on this lens: P(scored gate-passing probe) was 0.09 and 0.03-0.05 (v_external-data-training_dense-dorado-secondary_schedule.json, v_..._dense-primary-headrefit_schedule.json). This idea adds a stage and a gate before them, so its chain is strictly longer and its probability can only be lower. Second, its own gate is unlikely to pass. MEASURED here (4 CPU, pip ultrack 0.8.0, CBC solver; synthetic 64x256x256 clip, 300 well-separated gaussian nuclei/frame, sparse_zebrafish config): 20 frames took detect_foreground+robust_invert 107 s (5.4 s/frame, serial), segment 29 s, link 10 s and one 20-frame CBC window 41 s. Extrapolated, that is ~15-17 min per 100-frame clip at ~300 nodes/frame, and slower in real dense tissue (up to 781 nodes/frame, r2_critic.notes.md:12). Guess: 25-60 CPU-kernel-h for 199 clips, about 6-12 h wall on 5 parallel kernels, with a real risk that a dense chunk hits the 12 h limit. Even on these easy synthetic blobs, classical boundaries tracked only 271/300 nodes per frame (0.90). Gate (ii) needs a count/N_est of 0.95-1.25, and gate (i) needs >=70% of GT within 2.5 um. For reference, the hosts' own UNet-boundary Ultrack (dorado) reached 84% within 2.5 um and 97.2% within 7 um on 44b6, and it is still below our detector's 0.988 annotated recall (r2_critic.notes.md:15,20). Classical boundaries in the densest 6bba quartile, the target of this idea, should do worse (guess: P(gate) 0.3-0.4, below the idea's 0.5). The unet-simview route is not a real fallback: its preprocessing and normalisation are unpublished (ultrack_supplementary has only config.toml plus shell scripts that read precomputed layers), and public.czbiohub.org reachability from a Kaggle kernel is unverified (BROWSER_TODO #20). Implementation facts checked. Positive: pip install ultrack works (python >=3.11,<3.14). The pip gurobipy licence fails but ultrack falls back to CBC by itself, with no crash. Negative: the pip install pulls napari, zarr>=3 and torch>=2.0.1, so its first run on a Kaggle image is untested. Ultrack spawns worker processes, so it needs a main guard or a script file (my first run crashed without one). tools/build_dense_gt.py adds teacher nodes WITHOUT edges and uses Windows junctions, so the keep-edges merge is new code. Agents cannot push kernels (BRIEF sec.3), so the pilot, the debug iterations and 5 full-run kernels all go through Vitalii's laptop agent on the evening of 25 Sep, at the same time as #34/#35 scoring. Kaggle's concurrent CPU-session cap is unverified. The cited numbers check out: a_never 1,907 FN with 1,740 in 6bba (fn_anatomy_exp39.md l.9), 84% within 2.5 um (register_44b6_dorado.py docstring), the config values (config.toml: threshold 0.4, min/max area 300/25000, max_distance 10, weights -0.1, window 25, built for postgres and 25 workers). Probability chain, as written: pilot and debugging done by 25 Sep ~20:00 (0.75) x full run finished with no 12 h timeouts by 26 Sep 08:00 (0.8) x quality gate (0.35) x the downstream idea-1 fine-tune and OOS/lab gates (0.3) x dummy run and runtime OK (0.85), about 0.05. Without any gates it is ~0.45. Both are below 0.70.
fix_if_any: One repair makes this the best schedule variant of the dense-label family, but it still does not reach 0.70. (1) DECOUPLE it from dorado: use the Ultrack pseudo-labels on the 199 competition clips as the ONLY dense set for the idea-1 secondary fine-tune. This needs no Colab streaming, no external image extraction and no parity test, because the images are already mounted in Kaggle and the output is only geff files of a few MB per clip. (2) Pilot TODAY with ONE CPU kernel (internet ON) that runs 3 clips: 1 sparse 6bba, 1 densest-quartile 6bba, 1 44b6. Write it as a .py script with a main guard, set solver_name='CBC' explicitly, parallelise detect_foreground over frames (a pool of 4), and run the gate metrics IN-KERNEL against the mounted sparse GT: (i)-(iii) plus count/N_est. Record per-clip runtime. KILL on the pilot if the densest clip takes >40 min or its 2.5 um share is <60%. (3) If the pilot passes, run the full job as 5 CPU kernels, each owning a runtime-balanced list of ~40 clips sorted by nodes/frame, with a per-clip time_limit and resumable per-clip outputs, so a timeout loses one clip, not a chunk. (4) Treat the unet-simview route as optional: try one wget in the pilot kernel and use it only if it loads and gives an obviously better gate on the pilot. (5) The keep-edges merge is not needed for a detector-only secondary fine-tune; drop it from the critical path. (6) Keep the downstream gates of idea 1 (held-out 6bba videos, N_pred within +-2%). Even repaired: P(scored with honest gates) ~0.10-0.15, and P(executed and scored without gates) ~0.5-0.55.
realistic_public_gain: 0 on its own. Via ideas 1/2: about -0.003..+0.003, central ~0 (guess). The sibling value verdicts put ideas 1/2 at central -0.001/-0.002, and classical pseudo-labels are weaker in exactly the dense 6bba regime they are meant to fix. The expected realised gain by 29 Sep is ~0, because P(a scored gate-passing probe) is ~0.05.
realistic_private_gain: About -0.004..+0.003, central ~0 (guess). The two-embryo balance helps on paper, but pseudo-labels that under-segment dense tissue (0.90 count even on synthetic blobs) would teach the fine-tuned secondary to under-detect, which costs more on the unseen private embryos.
